title: Invariant open neighbourhoods inside invariant intersections for affine flat descent
statement:
Let $p:X\to S$ be a flat surjective morphism of affine schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-flat-morphism, def-weil-surjective-morphism]. Let $V\to X$ be a scheme, assume $V$ is quasi-separated [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism], and give it a descent datum $\varphi:V\times_S X\xrightarrow{\sim}X\times_S V$ over $X/S$ [def-pd-descent-datum, def-pc-fibre-product]. For a subset $F\subset |V|$, write $F\times_S X$ for its inverse image under $V\times_S X\to V$ and $X\times_S F$ for its inverse image under $X\times_S V\to V$. Then for every $v\in V$ there exist an open subscheme $W\subset V$ and a subset $E\subset |V|$ such that $v\in W\subset E$, $E$ is an intersection of a nonempty set-indexed family of quasi-compact opens of $V$, and
$$\varphi(W\times_S X)=X\times_S W,\qquad \varphi(E\times_S X)=X\times_S E.$$
The first equality is an equality of open subschemes and the second an equality of subsets.

source.place: Tags 0APA (lemma-first-observation), 0APB (lemma-second-observation), together with lemma-constructing-invariant-opens; applied to the cartesian groupoid associated to a descent datum by lemma-cartesian-equivalent-descent-datum

proof.text: Write R = V ×_S X, s = pr_V, q = pr_X and t = descentRelationTarget D. The transport law gives t ≫ V.hom = q. Define inversion i by the pullback lift of (t, s ≫ V.hom). Naturality [lem-pd-transport-left-naturality], the cocycle law [def-pd-descent-datum], and the identity law [lem-galois-descent-datum-diagonal-identity] give i ≫ s = t, i ≫ t = s and i ≫ i = id. Thus i is an isomorphism. Since p is between affines, [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-affine-schemes-affine] makes it affine. Base change [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence, lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change] makes s affine and flat; composition with i gives these properties for t. Both maps are quasi-compact by affineness. The section e = (id_V,V.hom) has e ≫ s = id and, by the same naturality and identity laws, e ≫ t = id.

source.place: Tag 0APF, lemma-cartesian-equivalent-descent-datum, specialized maps s and t; hypotheses of Tags 0APA and 0APB.

proof.text: For any subset $A\subset |V|$ put $\sigma(A)=t(s^{-1}(A))$. For each $z\in A$, [lem-pd-descent-orbit-saturated] applied to the transport defined by $\varphi$ gives $s^{-1}(O_z)=t^{-1}(O_z)$ for $O_z=t(s^{-1}(\{z\}))$. Since $\sigma(A)=\bigcup_{z\in A}O_z$ and inverse images commute with unions, $s^{-1}(\sigma(A))=t^{-1}(\sigma(A))$. Moreover $A\subset\sigma(A)$ by the identity section in step 1. These assertions also hold for $A=\varnothing$. Here the orbit lemma applies to precisely $R=V\times_S X$ and the target $t$ defined by universal transport, not to an unrelated action.

source.place: Tag 03LO, lemma-constructing-invariant-opens (1), using the existing singleton-orbit interface and unions.

proof.text: Choose an affine open $Q$ containing $v$ by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]; it is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. Apply [lem-a1-flat-relation-qc-image-intersections] to $Q$. Thus $K=\sigma(Q)$ is quasi-compact and closed under generalization, and there is a quasi-compact open $H$ containing $K$. Step 2 gives $v\in Q\subseteq K$ and invariance of $K$.

source.place: Tag 0APA: apply the quasi-compact image interface to Q.

proof.text: Apply [lem-a1-flat-relation-invariant-open-complement] to these $s,t,K,H$. Its saturation axiom and common section are supplied by steps 1–2. For $Z=V\setminus H$ and $T=\sigma(Z)$ it gives the invariant open $W=V\setminus\overline T$ with $v\in K\subseteq W\subseteq H$.

Put $E=\sigma(H)$. By step 2, $E$ is invariant and $W\subseteq H\subseteq E$. Apply [lem-a1-flat-relation-qc-image-intersections] again, now to $H$. It gives a quasi-compact containing open $H_2$ and expresses $E$ as the intersection of the nonempty set of quasi-compact opens of $H_2$ containing $E$, all quasi-compact open in $V$.

source.place: Tag 0APA: apply the same image interface to H.

proof.text: The complement lemma supplies equality of inverse images of the underlying subset of W; extensionality of opens turns this into the required equality of inverse-image opens. Saturation supplies equality of the inverse images of E. The image lemma gives E as an intersection of subsets which are open and compact in V. Replace each such open subset by the corresponding element of V.Opens. This identifies its nonempty family with the family of U : V.Opens contained in H₂, compact, and containing E. Extensionality gives the required doubly indexed intersection. No change of a target statement or definition is involved.

proof_origin.place: Tags 03LO (lemma-constructing-invariant-opens), 0APA (lemma-first-observation), 0APB (lemma-second-observation); the inclusion Q⊂W⊂H⊂σ(H) implements the application in More Groupoids Tag 0APK.
